title: InferScale: GPU-Native KV Injection for Personalized LLM Serving
event_hint: GPU-resident semantic memory retrieval with position-independent KV injection
problem: Persistent personalized memory is repeatedly retrieved as prompt text and re-prefilled, so TTFT rises with the amount of reused memory even across requests. Prefix caching cannot directly reuse dynamically assembled facts at changing prompt positions.
mechanism: InferScale stores each memory fact's semantic embedding and pre-RoPE KV representation on GPU, retrieves relevant facts with a GPU-resident ANN index, applies Chunked RoPE at serving-time positions, and injects KV directly into vLLM's paged cache through the KV-connector interface. Context-Window Encoding encodes each fact with a small preceding-conversation window while caching only the target fact, recovering cross-fact accuracy without serving-time recomputation or model fine-tuning.

evidence.claim: On Llama-3.1-8B, InferScale TTFT rose only 4% from k=5 to k=50 (16.6–17.3 ms), versus 106% for Mem0 (33.2–68.3 ms).
evidence.condition: LoCoMo; retrieval budget k=5 to k=50

evidence.claim: At k=50, InferScale reduced TTFT by 72–79% (3.6–4.8x) relative to prompt injection.
At k=50, InferScale reached 60.3% LoCoMo accuracy versus 63.3% for Mem0, without serving-time recomputation.
Under concurrent load, InferScale delivered 3.7–4.5x Mem0 throughput at 100 users.
Offloading a 1.8–4.8 GB per-conversation KV store to host DRAM added about 3 ms engine TTFT; at k=50 end-to-end query-to-first-token remained 2.3x faster than Mem0 (approximately 100 ms vs 236 ms).
evidence.condition: Llama-3.1-8B; k=50; PCIe streaming from host DRAM

evaluation_context: InferScale is implemented as a vLLM KV-connector plugin and evaluated on LoCoMo with three open-weight models, comparing against Mem0 prompt injection across retrieval budgets and concurrent users. It uses GPU-resident vector/KV stores and also tests host-DRAM offload; no engine modification or fine-tuning is required.
limitations: Independent fact encoding omits cross-fact interactions and remains an approximation; Context-Window Encoding recovers much but not all Mem0 accuracy (60.3% versus 63.3% at k=50). GPU-resident indices and KV stores consume memory, while host offload adds PCIe latency and depends on capacity/bandwidth. Results use LoCoMo, three open-weight models, vLLM, and one memory-system baseline; broader models, workloads, cache eviction behavior, and multi-node network costs are not shown (inference).
project_relevance: InferScale is a concrete KV-network/runtime primitive: keep reusable context on the accelerator, retrieve by semantic identity, apply serving-time position transforms, and bypass repeated prefill. For TPN and serving evaluation, measure TTFT versus retrieval budget, PCIe/network bytes, KV-store placement, concurrency throughput, and accuracy separately; the method complements rather than replaces cross-node KV-cache scheduling (inference).
